note: The graded evaluation protocol, stated where you can read it. The verifier trains the frozen decoder itself on the tokens your plan names, takes the parameter snapshot its own trainer produced at budget exhaustion, and evaluates that snapshot on the frozen held-out FineWeb10B validation split with the settings below. Editing this file does not change what the verifier computes; the verifier always recomputes unsmoothed. It only changes what the verifier observes you declared, and a declared value other than none is graded as readout smoothing and scores zero.
objective: mean token-level cross entropy in nats, computed by a forward pass of the trained snapshot over the held-out split
_target_note: 3.28 is the substrate's admission bar for a full record run and is quoted here for orientation only. It is not this slot's bar: this slot grades a fixed 20971520 token budget, which is far short of a record run, and it is scored on the loss reached inside that budget rather than on clearing 3.28.

heldout.shape_is_published_bytes_are_not: The SHAPE of the graded split is stated here because you cannot judge fold risk without it. Its BYTES are not, they live verifier-side at tests/heldout_spec.json, and no pool slice id resolves to them. The split is partitioned into the two folds above and the whole-split loss is the token-weighted mean of the two fold losses.
heldout.folds_are_not_balanced_against_each_othe: The two folds hold equal sequence counts and are contiguous halves of the split, so they carry different text and deliberately unequal composition. Because max(fold) is always at least the whole-split loss, the sustained-across-folds condition is strictly stronger than the whole-split condition, and a mixture that wins on average by trading one fold against the other is refused by construction.
heldout.probe_relationship: environment/corpus_spec.json dev_probe is a slice of a FineWeb10B TRAIN shard that carries no pool slice. It is the same corpus but a different, much smaller sample carrying different bytes, and it is drawn from the train side rather than the validation side. environment/harness.py reports the ratio of held-out tokens to probe tokens, because an improvement measured on the probe is being extrapolated by that factor onto a split you never see.
